details:
VRChat appears to deliberately prevent clicking any button that you can't see, i.e. a button on your left while your head is turned to the right.  This makes some sense as a deliberate choice; you might not realise that your click is going to do something, if you're just gesturing off to the side with your hand and clicking the trigger to gesture with a finger, or something.  However, I'm always running into the situation of turning to face a control panel, pointing my cursor at a button, and then turning my head towards what that button *is going to affect* (which is often in another direction!), and THEN clicking, in order to watch the effect take place.   And when I try to do that, I can't!  The click does nothing, until I turn my head back towards the button, THEN click, THEN turn my head back, having just missed the transition.

This sounds intractable, but I think there's actually a simple solution:  allow clicking of any button which *is already highlighted*, and only allow HIGHLIGHTING of buttons that are on screen!   This way, both scenarios work as desired:  accidentally pointing towards a button that you can't see *still* won't let you interact with it without looking, but looking towards a button, pointing your cursor at it, THEN turning your head away, will work as expected (the button remains clickable because its highlighting happened while you were looking directly at it).

If that's too complex, honestly, I'd accept just an option in the settings to allow *all* out-of-sight clicks, and I'll just live with the consequences; I think the false positives would happen far far less often than I deal with the false negatives, I'd happily opt into that trade.
title: Allow clicking buttons while looking away
